::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Febry 27 1899  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** The Rev. Canon Geoffrey Curtis[^1]
:::

Dear [Sir](people/person_2083.qmd)
I am much obliged for your letter, with the curious particulars about the Bartons.  The cow is delightful!  

But Manydown is not a mistake, it is near Basingstoke, and (I believe) held on the tenure of receiving the Winchester scholars if the plague was in the city.  I have known many of the family of Bigg, who two generations ago, took the surname of Wither, on inheriting Tangier Park from the family of [George Wither](people/person_1686.qmd), the Poet.  The crest is a demi hare, with an ear of Big (barley) in its mouth.  I cannot recollect the shield, but I rather think that it had the big or barley in it.  I wonder whether yours is the same.

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

That was a bad pen so I will take a better one for an autograph
Charlotte Mary Yonge

---

[^1]: Pasted into a copy of *John Keble's Parishes* (1899) with the ownership stamp of Matthew R. Bigge and the bookplate and monogrammed binding of John Tricks Spalding.
